note: The Leningrad Codex reads hadad (as also 1 Chr 1:30); the KJV follows printed Hebrew editions that read hadar, a dalet/resh confusion.

kjv: by their (Ishmael's sons') towns, and by their castles
mine: by their (Ishmael's sons') settlements and their encampments
note: Hebrew hatserim are unwalled settlements and tirot are nomadic encampments or stone enclosures; "towns" and "castles" suggest fortified urban life foreign to these tribes.

kjv: he (Ishmael) died in the presence of all his brethren
mine: He (Ishmael) settled down in defiance of all his kinsmen
note: The verb nafal ("fell") here means settled or camped (fulfilling 16:12, where the same phrase al-pene kol-ehav is used); the KJV takes it as "died", which the verb does not mean here.
The elliptical lamah zeh anokhi ("why this, I?") is obscure; it is often read as despair over living (cf. 27:46), while the KJV keeps it vague.
Hebrew yodea tsayid, "knowing game"; "cunning" meant skillful in 1611 but now implies craftiness.
Hebrew tam means whole, sound or blameless; in context it contrasts the settled, even-tempered Jacob with the wild Esau. "Plain" now suggests homely looks or simplicity.
Hebrew tsayid means any hunted game; "venison" in 1611 meant game generally but now means deer meat only. The same applies throughout ch.27.
